findings.title: ensure_loaded! runs under global LOAD_MUTEX for every fallback locale on every request
findings.body: set_locale now calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every controller request, which iterates up to 3 locales (user, site default, en) and calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for each, acquiring LOAD_MUTEX each time. Although load_locale returns early if already loaded, this still means every request now runs the mutex-synchronized membership check 2-3x instead of once, adding unnecessary contention/overhead especially under multi-threaded Puma/Unicorn with many concurrent requests.

findings.title: translate still only loads config.locale, not fallback locales
findings.body: The patched translate method only ensures config.locale is loaded (load_locale(config.locale)), but with fallbacks now enabled via I18n::Backend::Fallbacks, a translation lookup for the current locale may need to fall through to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en translations which are never explicitly loaded by this accelerator. Since Base#load_translations is overridden to require explicit loading of files, translations for fallback locales other than config.locale may never actually be loaded into the backend unless something else triggers it (e.g. the controller's set_locale calling ensure_loaded! for all fallbacks). This creates a fragile coupling: translate() depends on an external before_filter to pre-load fallback locales, so any I18n.t call made before set_locale runs (e.g. during console/rake tasks, background jobs, or early boot) can silently return missing-translation results instead of falling back correctly.

findings.title: SiteSetting access during initializer load order risk
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale at lookup time, which is fine lazily, but note this initializer unconditionally overwrites I18n.fallbacks for all environments (removed previously environment-specific config.i18n.fallbacks = true toggles). There's no longer any way to disable fallbacks per-environment as previously supported in production/profile configs, which were removed. If fallbacks are undesired in some environment (e.g. test, to catch missing translation keys precisely), this is now a global behavior change with no opt-out, differing from previous per-environment configurability.
